## Summary Two template-ref cases compile incorrectly to Vapor: 1. `ref="child"` on a component is emitted as a component prop (`{ ref: () => "child" }`) instead of a template ref. The parent's ref stays `null`, so `defineExpose` values are unreachable. 2. `ref="items"` on an element inside `v-for` is emitted as `_setRef(n, "items")` without the `refInFor` flag, so the ref is not an array: `items.value.length` is `0` after mount. The output is the same through `@vizejs/native` `compileSfc(src, { vapor: true })`, so Vite users are affected too. ## Environment - `vize` 0.432.0 (npm), `vue` / `@vue/compiler-sfc` 3.6.0-rc.10 for comparison - macOS 26.4.1 arm64, Node v26.10.0, npm 11.19.1 ## Reproduction ```sh mkdir repro && cd repro cat > App.vue <<'VUE' VUE cat > Child.vue <<'VUE' VUE npx vize@0.432.0 build --no-config -o out App.vue && sed -n '/^function render/,/^}/p' out/App.js ``` ## Actual ```js const _setRef = _ctx.vaporTemplateRefSetter || _createTemplateRefSetter() const n0 = _createComponentWithFallback(_component_Child, { ref: () => ("child") }, null, true) const n1 = _createFor(() => (3), (_for_item0) => { const n3 = t0() _setRef(n3, "items") … ``` Mounted (Vue 3.6.0-rc.10, `createVaporApp`), `

` shows `undefined / 0`. ## Expected `

` shows `world / 3`. `@vue/compiler-sfc` emits a template ref for the component and passes the in-for flag (dev, non-inline): ```js const n0 = _createComponent(_ctx.Child) _setStaticTemplateRef(n0, "child") … _setTemplateRef(n3, "items", true) ```
